svg.title: Pointers and references, with real addresses
svg.text: Pointers and references, with real addresses
the three symbols the order book code is full of: * -> &

g.text: Every object lives at an address. An Order is 48 bytes: S1 starts at byte 1000, S2 right after it at 1048.
memory: a long row of numbered bytes

g.text: Order* maker = lvl.head; A POINTER is a variable that holds an address. maker holds 1000. Nothing was copied.

g.text: maker->qty means: go to the address in maker, then take the field qty. It reads 40 from S1.

g.text: maker->qty -= 40; This changes S1 ITSELF, in place. Everyone who points at S1 now sees qty = 0.

g.text: A reference (the & in Level& lvl) is a second name for an object that already exists. No copy is made.

g.text: & = a second NAME for asks_[101]. The book changes ✓

text.font-family: DejaVu Sans Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

g.text: no & = a COPY. Only the copy changes; the book does not ✗
pointer: can be null, can be re-pointed, uses ->
reference: never null, fixed for life, uses a dot
